_source: REPO-LOCAL OVERRIDE (autosql). Copied from the plugin's data/gates.json on 2026-08-22 and extended with a `design` gate, per Evan's wrapup item 4 answer under GA-6: 'Make it a real checkpoint'. Repo-local because tracker.mjs resolves gates.json from .autodev/data/ first and falls back to the plugin — so this survives a plugin update, which a patch to the plugin cache would not. When the plugin ships its own design gate, delete this file and this repo inherits it again.

spec_ready.name: spec_ready
spec_ready.question: Is this spec ready to build from? Read the acceptance criteria: are they testable, is the scope what you actually want, and is anything missing that you would regret discovering after the build?

keyholder.instructions: Read the ticket's spec and acceptance criteria. If you cannot tell what 'done' looks like from the ACs alone, the spec is not ready — send it back with the question that stumped you.

merge.name: merge
merge.question: Should this change land on the shared branch now? The automated checks are green and review findings are resolved or waived — do you accept those waivers and want this code in the codebase?

keyholder.instructions: Open the PR. Check the review findings and any waivers; a green suite is necessary but not sufficient. If a waiver makes you uneasy, hold and say why.

accept.name: accept
accept.question: Is this what you actually asked for? Compare the finished work against your original intent — not against the spec. Does it do what you meant, and would you show it to someone?

keyholder.instructions: Use the thing, do not just read about it. Follow the acceptance package's numbered checklist against the running product. Judge intent-conformance: the spec can be satisfied while the intent is not.

deploy.name: deploy
deploy.question: Ship this to production now? Verification is green — is the timing right (no one mid-demo, someone reachable if it breaks), and is the rollback path confirmed?

keyholder.instructions: Confirm the rollback path exists before saying yes. If you would not want to be paged about this change tonight, hold it until you would.

sp_decide.name: sp_decide
sp_decide.question: The research is in — options, evidence, and a recommendation. Do you accept the recommendation, pick another option, or send it back for more digging?

keyholder.instructions: Read the synthesis, not just the recommendation. Ruling 29: a spike's decision_authority can dial this per spike (autonomous | recommend-and-wait | auto-unless-contested) via the ticket's per-gate override; the shop policy here is the default.

ex_decide.name: ex_decide
ex_decide.question: The experiment window closed and the numbers are in. Against the decision rule you set at frame time: keep it, kill it, or iterate?

keyholder.instructions: Read the readout numbers against YOUR framed decision rule — the rule's verdict is a recommendation, not a clearance. If the numbers are ambiguous, iterate is an honest answer.

compliance.name: compliance
compliance.question: Does this change meet the team's compliance obligations — data handling, audit trail, accessibility, regulatory requirements — with the evidence attached, before it goes any further?

keyholder.instructions: Check the compliance checklist for this change class. Every obligation gets an explicit yes-with-evidence or a named blocker; 'probably fine' is a hold, not a pass.

design.name: design
design.question: Is this the look you want built? You are seeing the screen as a drawing, before anyone writes it. Layout, wording, how loudly it says what it needs to say — say it now, while changing it is layout work rather than rework.

keyholder.instructions: Open the mock and drive it — do not judge it from a description. Click every state it offers, and look at it on the monitor you will actually use. If a drawing cannot settle something, the design brief's open-questions section is where to answer it.

_policy_values: human (the human's call; an agent MAY clear on their behalf, recorded honestly as agent:...(on-behalf:<human>,<why>)) | human:strict (ONLY a confirmed human — on-behalf refused, so the gate truly holds and unattended work stops there) | auto-when-green | unattended
